assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins is a physical mechanism stated in quantitative terms: distance and driving-force dependence, tunneling pathways, reorganization energy, measured with time-resolved kinetics in engineered metalloproteins. It underlies respiration and photosynthesis, which is the biological energy conversion I work on, and it is original and conceptually clear.
assessment.attribution: A two-person line of work with sustained joint authorship over decades. Priority relative to Marcus theory (already recognized), Hopfield, and the Dutton and Moser work on protein electron-transfer rules is a real allocation question, but the supplied credit gives a clean two-laureate configuration.
assessment.maturity: Four decades of independent confirmation, now textbook, including hopping and multistep tunneling and biological relevance. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: How much of the conceptual framework should be credited to the Dutton and Moser group, which is not in the supplied credit.
Whether the committee sees this as applied Marcus theory, already honored, rather than a new discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer connects directly to proton pumping and redox catalysis in enzymes such as cytochrome c oxidase. Theory of concerted versus stepwise transfer plus molecular electrocatalysis gives a mechanistic vocabulary for water oxidation, nitrogen and oxygen chemistry, and enzymes.
assessment.attribution: Mayer on bond-weakening and thermochemistry, Nocera on model systems and artificial photosynthesis, and Hammes-Schiffer on the theory. Thomas J. Meyer made early foundational contributions, so the three-name limit forces a hard choice and priority is contestable.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely confirmed in experiment and theory. Some applied claims, such as the cobalt phosphate catalyst, have been debated, so I would credit the mechanism rather than devices.
uncertainties: The line of work is broad rather than one discovery, and some may see it as a framework more than a single attributable finding.
Whether Meyer's priority should displace one of the three proposed names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is a central chemical enigma, reducing N2 to ammonia at a unique metal cofactor. Crystal structures of the MoFe protein and FeMo cofactor, the interstitial carbide, and the mechanistic work on the E4 state gave a physical picture of a hard multielectron, proton-coupled process. Importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Rees was decisive for structures and cofactor, Einsle for the carbide and high-resolution work, and Seefeldt (with Dean) for the kinetics and mechanism. Dean, Ribbe and others have claims, so the three-name limit makes the allocation contentious.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well established; the full catalytic mechanism, including how N2 binds, is still incompletely resolved, so some aspects may be premature.
uncertainties: Mechanism of N2 binding and reduction is not settled.
Allocation among five credited people, with the Haber-Bosch prize already given.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers gave diffraction before radiation damage and enabled time-resolved structures of reactions, including photosystem and photoreceptor dynamics. It makes mechanisms visible, which I value, and it opens time-resolved structural enzymology.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the 2011 proof of principle, Fromme the membrane protein and photosystem applications, and Schlichting the time-resolved work. Hajdu's earlier conceptual contribution and the wider team make attribution difficult, and the method depends on facilities.
assessment.maturity: Method is well confirmed; the scientific payoff from time-resolved biology is still developing, so recognition could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Whether the breakthroughs are mostly method development with a still-limited number of mechanistic discoveries.
Fair credit for Hajdu, Neutze and Spence is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Biomolecular condensates organize cell chemistry without membranes. The physical-chemistry framing, with liquid-liquid phase separation, multivalency and sticker-spacer models, is a fundamental advance in cell organization and has been highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman made the original P-granule observation, and Rosen provided multivalent-interaction biochemistry. Pappu and Mittag contributed physics, so five credited names exceed the limit and the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly maturing but still debated: the physiological relevance of phase separation for many assemblies, and artefacts in cells, remain arguments. It may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Physiological significance versus in vitro behavior is still disputed.
Allocation among five names, with biology-versus-chemistry fit questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors perform programmable single-nucleotide chemistry on DNA through cytosine and adenine deaminase fusions, without double-strand cleavage. It is an inventive chemical-biology idea with immediate therapeutic and research use, and original in concept.
assessment.attribution: Liu's group developed it; Komor developed the cytosine editor and Gaudelli the adenine editor. This gives a clean configuration, though Nishida and Kondo have an independent early claim to the cytidine deaminase system.
assessment.maturity: Clinical translation is under way and the method has been widely replicated, but long-term safety data are limited. Timely, though perhaps early compared with the rest of the list.
uncertainties: Whether the Nishida and Kondo priority claim is adequately handled.
A genome-editing prize was already given to CRISPR, and the committee may see this as a derivative step.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR with relaxation and residual-dipolar-coupling methods gives structure and dynamics of large biomolecules in solution, and so connects structure to kinetics and mechanism. Very large impact on biochemistry.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Clore, Kay, Wagner and Palmer all made decisive contributions. A three-person split excludes at least two with strong claims, and the Wuthrich prize already covers the foundations.
assessment.maturity: Mature and extensively confirmed over decades. Recognition is timely if allocation can be resolved.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among five, and overlap with the 2002 NMR prize.
Whether the field is seen as a continuation rather than a new discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The spliceosome structures and catalytic mechanism describe a large dynamic RNA-protein machine that performs two-step ribozyme-like chemistry. A mechanistic and structural landmark for RNA biochemistry and cryo-EM.
assessment.attribution: Lührmann on biochemistry and the spliceosome composition, and Shi and Stark on cryo-EM structures. Nguyen is credited for the structures, which makes the contribution partly team-based, but a three-name set is workable.
assessment.maturity: Structures are confirmed by several groups, though the dynamic mechanism across all steps is still being filled in.
uncertainties: Credit relative to earlier work on splicing, which is already recognized.
How much of the machine is understood mechanistically rather than structurally.
